AVALON CITY COUNCIL MEETING WHICH WILL ALSO INCLUDE

  TUESDAY, JULY 19, 2022— 5:00 P.M.
  410 AVALON CANYON ROAD
  THIS VIRTUAL MEETING IS HELD PURSUANT TO AB 361
  AGENDA

  In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
  meeting, please contact Denise Radde, City Clerk (310) 510-0220. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting
  will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35.
  102-35104 ADA Title II). All public records relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the
  public inspection at the time the records are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members of the City Council.
  Such records shall be available at City Hall located at 410 Avalon Canyon Rd.

Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of California
Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared state of emergency
wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or recommended, the CITY OF
AVALONS CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL GENERALLY
BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC REMOTELY. The general public may attend the meeting in
the Council Chambers however must adhere to social distancing requirements. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes while practicing social
distancing.

Council Chambers are open to a maximum 30 members of the general public. Once the Council
Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in Oral
Communication and address the City Council on an agenda item in person by waiting in the City
Hall Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time at the appropriate time. No one will be
admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. Additionally,
the general public may participate in Oral Communication and address the City Council on an
agenda items by providing comments via Zoom or by sending comments to
ask@cityofavalon.com.

  The meeting can be viewed:
  On local cable: Catalina Broadband Solutions channel 3
  Streaming Online: www.cityofavalon.com/meetings

3.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16. 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and
  that as a result of the COVID-1 9 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every
  thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming August
  16, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency! meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Appointments to Fill Three Terms on the Planning Commission
  The Planning Commission is a seven person commission with one optional alternate
  member. Planning Commissioners serve four year terms. Three Planning Commissioner
  terms have expired.
  Recommended Action
  Discuss applications received, consider the recommendation of Mayor Ann H. Marshall,
  and make an appointment for three individuals to serve as Planning Commissioner for
  new terms, expiring June 30, 2026.

7.  Appointing a Mayor Pro-Tem
  The City Clerk will call for nominations for Mayor Pro Tem. If there is more than one
  nomination, voting for those nominated will be conducted. The person receiving the most
  votes will be declared the Mayor Pro Tem.
  Recommended Action
  Nominate and vote on a member of the City Council to serve as the Mayor Pro Tem.

8.  Audit Committee
  There are two members of City Council that sit on the audit committee. Their job is to
  review all warrants that go before the City Council for approval.
  Recommended Action
  Appoint two members of the City Council to serve as the Audit Committee.

9.  Avalon Municipal Hospital Board of Trustees
  City Council appoints itself to serve as the Hospital Board of Trustees and appoints
  one of its members to serve as the Chairman.
  Recommended Action
  Appoint the City Council to serve as the Avalon Municipal Hospital Board of
  Trustees and appoint a Chairman of the Board.

PUBLIC HEARING

10.  Appeal Planning Commission Action 22-01 of PC #2783 Approving a Setback Variance
  at 261 E. Whittley
  On April 20,2022, the Planning Commission of the City of Avalon took action on a request
  for approval of a Site Plan and a Setback Variance at 261 E. Whittley for the ongoing
  remodel of a duplex in the Medium Density Residential zone. On May 3, 2022 Charles
  Canby, and other surrounding property owners, filed a timely appeal of the Planning
  Commission’s decision, requesting that the City Council hear the Project at a public
  hearing. Public hearings were held on June 8 and June 21, 2022 and the item was
  continued to July 19, 2022.
  Recommended Action
  1. Continue the Public Hearing to hear public comment. 2. Close the Public Hearing. 3.
  Discuss and determine appropriate action by either: a.) Affirming the action of the
  Planning Commission; b.) Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other
 CITY COUNCILIHOSPITAL AGENDA
JULY 19, 2022
PAGES

  evidence evidence upon which the Commission made its decision, and after receiving
  such take such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; c.) Refer the
  matter back to the Commission, with or without instructions for further proceedings; or d.)
  Continue the matter for hearing on another date before itself, considered de novo. (Avalon
  Municipal Code Section 9-8.601)

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed
by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result of the
COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21. which provided that the
exceptions contained in EO N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required under AB 361

Under AB 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a
Governor-proclaimed state of emergency, which the City Council will consider in their
determination, and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; or

65059.00000\3452048 1.1
   2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the

having members of the public attend council meetings at locations where council members are
in attendance due to their desire to avoid exposure to COVID-19 poses an imminent risk to the
health or safety of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: The 2018-2021 Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) between the
City of Avalon and its five labor associations: International Association of Firefighters Local
2295 (IAFF), Avalon Harbor Employee Association (AHEA), Avalon Municipal Employee
Association (AMEA), Management and Confidential Employees were adopted on July 16,
2019.

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the financial impact of statewide shutdowns, emergency
modifications were made to the MOUs on August 4, 2020. These modifications included:
  1. All uniform allowances eliminated. Uniforms would only be purchased on an as needed
  basis.
  2. Travel reimbursements, also known as commuter book reimbursements (2 annually),
  eliminated. (Partially reinstated on December 31, 2021.)
  3. Education reimbursements eliminated.
  4. Floating Holidays (2 days/16 hours of paid time off) eliminated.
  5. When calculating overtime, hours worked” would only be defined as hours actually
  worked. Vacation hours would no longer be factored into overtime calculations.
  6. Accumulation of comp time was eliminated.
  7. All longevity increases frozen. No retroactive pay would be accumulated.
  8. Employees could no longer cash out administrative paid time off. A maximum 30 to 40
  hours would be carried over year to year.
  9. Volunteer Drill Pay, Special Drill Pay were restricted and available only at the Fire
  Chiefs discretion.
  10.Training and Leave Pay, and Association Representative Leave is eliminated.
  11. Cost of Living and Classification/Compensation Studies were postponed.
 Effective March 17, 2020 all step increases were frozen for all employees and a notification
was made indicating no retroactive pay would be accumulated during this time period.

These modifications resulted in significant cost savings and helped the City to remain solvent
during a very tumultuous time.

In February 2022. the City Manager began meeting with the City’s labor associations/unions to
negotiate revised MOUs for the 2022-2025 contract period. On April 4. 2022 the City Manager
received letters from Service Employees International Union, CTW, CCL Local 721 (SEIU) on
behalf of the AMEA and AHEA indicating the association’s interest in unionizing. A
determination was made to hold an election by mail in ballot on May 9, 20222. The election
concluded on June 3, 2022 with ballots opened and counted on June 6, 2022. Both the AHEA
and AMEA members voted to join SEIU as two different uns SEIU Harbor Unit and SEIU
  —

Municipal Employee Unit.

The City Manager and SEIU representatives negotiated revised contract terms restoring the
benefits rescinded in the emergency revisions. Additionally, to counter the wage freeze that
has been in place since 2020, the new MOUs provide all employees covered by the MOUs a
wage increase annually for the terms of the agreements. Per negotiations, once ratified, any
wage increases will be retroactive to June 29, 2022.

The SEIU Harbor Unit and SEUI Municipal Employee Unit MOUs align with IAFF, Management
and Confidential/Unrepresented labor associations MOUs approved and adopted by the City
Council on May 3, 2022.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Fiscal implications of these MOUs have been integrated into the Fiscal
Year 2022-2023 Budget.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Fiscal and organizational stability.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
current MOUs with the SEIU Harbor Unit or the SEIU Municipal Employee Unit.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

employed in a non-exempt position. A catastrophic illness or injury is defined as a serious illness,

  4. A period of incapacity that is long-term due to a condition for which treatment may be

  either for restorative surgery after an accident or other injury, or for a chronic condition such

Employees International Union, Local 721 (referred to hereinafter as “Union”) and the
employees covered herein; to provide orderly means of attempting to resolve misunderstandings

understanding of the parties reached as a result of good faith negotiations regarding the wages,
hours and other terms and conditions of employment of the employee cover hereby.

activities of employee organizations and the equal alternative right of employees to reftise to form.
join or participate in employee organization activities. No employee shall be intimidated, coerced,

of the employer-employee relationship, including recruitment. hiring, upgrading. training.
promotion. transfer, discipline, layoff, recall. and termination.

  WORK SCHEDULE

The City’s Department Supervisors will assign work and schedule employees in accordance with
the requirements, responsibilities and needs of the City. It is the purview of the Department
Supervisor to determine the hours of work and change work schedules and assignments. Any
changes to an employee’s work schedule, unless due to a state of emergency, will he provided to
the employee with a minimum of 24 hours’ notice.

  ALTERNATE WORK SCHEDULE

Upon supervisor approval, employees may be permitted to work a “9/80” work schedule, where
the employee alternates between a calendar week of four 9—hour days and a calendar week of four
9—hour days plus one 8—hour day. Upon approval of such a request, the City will adjust the start
and end of the employee’s workweek (as opposed to calendar week) to begin and end at the 4—
hour mark of the 8—hour day. The City shall further determine the actual days to be worked for
any employee working a “9/80” schedule.

  HOLIDAYS

Employees shall not be required to be in attendance on paid holidays.

  GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE

A grievance shall he any matter for which appeal is not otherwise provided or prohibited.
concerning:
  I. A dispute ahoul the interpretation or application of this MOU and Personnel Rules and
  Regulations:
  A. Informal Grievance Procedure:
  An employee who has a problem or complaint should first try to get it settled
  through discussion with his immediate supervisor without undue delay within one
  —

  or two workdays of the event grieved. If, after this discussion, he/she does not
  believe the problem has been satisfactorily resolved, he/she shall have the right to
  promptly discuss it with the supervisors immediate superior, if any, in the
  administrative service. Every effort should be made without delay to find an
  acceptable solution by informal means at the lowest possible level of supervision.
  If the employee, or the Union, is not in agreement with the decision reached by
  discussion, he/she shall then have the right to file a formal grievance in writing
  within ten (10) calendar days after receiving the informal decision of his/her
  supervisor or the supervisor’s immediate superior on matters within the statutory
  scope of representations.
  B. Formal Grievance Procedure:
  1. First level of Review: A grievance shall bc presented in writing to the
  employee’s immediate supervisor within ten (10) calendar days of the informal
  process decision or of the event giving rise to the grievance, whichever is later.
  Thc supervisor shall render hisher decision and comments in writing and return
  them to the employee within ten (10) calendar days after receiving the
  grievance. In the event that the super\ isor does not render a decision within the
  10 days or within a mutually agreed upon extension of the timcline, the
  employee has the right to move the grievance up to the next level of review.
  2. Further Level or Levels of Review as Appropriate: The supervisors immediate
  superior receiving the grievance shall review it, render his/her decision and
  comments in writing, and return them to the employee within ten (10) calendar
  days after receiving the appeal. In the event that the supervisor does not render
  a decision within the 10 days or within a mutually agreed upon extension of the
  timelinc, the employee has the right to move the grievance up to the next level
  of review.
  3. Department Review: The Department I-lead receiving the grievance, or his/her
  designated representative, should discuss the grievance with the employee, his

  21
   SEIU AVALON MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEE’S

  representative, if any, and with other appropriate persons. The Department
  Head shall render his/her decision and comments in writing, and return them to
  the employee within ten (10) calendar days after receiving the appeal. If the
  employee, or the union, does not agree with the decision reached, or if no
  answer has been received within ten (10) calendar days, he may present the
  appeal in writing to the City Manager. Failure of the employee to take further
  action within twenty (20) days after receipt of the decision, or wit]iin a total of
  twenty (20) days if no decisions is rendered, will constitute withdrawal of the
  grievance.
  4. City Manager: The City Manager or his/her designee should discuss the
  grievance with the employee, his/her representative, if any, and with other
  appropriate persons. The City Manager may designate an “investigation
  committee.” or an officer not in the normal line of supervision, to advise
  him/her concerning the grievance. The appointing power shall render a decision
  in writing to the employee within twenty (20) days after receiving the grievance.
C. Grievance Arbitration:
  I. Within ten (10) working days of the receipt of the City Manager’s final
  decision, the Union may request arbitration by tiling a written request. The
  request for arbitration shall be in writing to the Department Head with a copy
  sent to the Personnel Officer/City Manager.
  2. If either the City or the Union so requests, the arbitrator shall hear the mcrits of
  any issue raised regarding the arbitrability of a grievance first. No hearing on
  the merits of the grievance shall be conducted until the issue of arbitrability has
  been decided.
  3. The parties shall request a list of five (5) arbitrators, within ten (10) working
  days aftcr receipt of the employee’s request for arbitration. from the California
  State Mediation and Conciliation Service.
  4. Within five (5) working days of receipt of the list, the parties shall mutually
  agree upon the person on the list who shall be the Arbitrator. If one person is
  not mutually agreed upon. the parties shall within five (5) days after receipt of
  the list of names alternately’ strike names from such list with the last remaining
  name to he the person serving as Arbitrator. The party having first choice to
  strike a name from the list shall be determined by lot.
  5. The City and the Union shall share the fees and expenses of the arbitrator and
  the certified court reporter equally. The services of the certified court reporter
  are optional. Both parties must agree if the certified court reporter is to be
  employed and that the cost shall be equally shared. Financial responsibility shall
  be established before the selection of an arbitrator. All other expenses shall be
  borne by the party incurring them, and neither party shall be responsible for the
  expense of witnesses called by the other. However, if either party declines the
  use ofa court reporter, the party requesting the court reporter shall pay the entire
  cost of employing the court reporter.
  a. If the Union cannot afford to pay the fees and expenses of the
  arbitration. the City’ may offer to provide a zero interest loan to the
  Union. Accumulated Union dues would pay down the loan monthly
  until the final balance is remitted.

  Personnel Rules and Regulations.
  7. Decision: The decision of the arbitrator shall be made in writing within tlurty
  (30) working days of the close of the hearing or the submission of written briefs.
  The decision of the arbitrator shall he final.

  I. The nine limits specified above may be cxtended to a definite date by mutual

  CATASTROPHIC LEAVE

A permanent employee may be granted a Catastrophic Leave for up 8 weeks, if the employee or
eligible family member has suffered a catastrophic illness or injury, and exhausted all applicable
accrued paid time. An eligible family member includes the employee’s spouse, parent, child,
sibling, grandparent, grandchild; in-laws and step-relatives in these relationships; and other
persons residing in the employee’s household for whom there is a personal obligation.

Catastrophic illness or injury is a serious non—work-related health condition which incapacitates the
employee, or their eligible family member, and which creates a financial hardship because the employee
has exhausted their sick and vacation leave, as well as any compensatoi’y time off if employed in a non-
exempt position. A catastrophic illness or injury is defined as a serious illness, injury, impairment. or
physical or menial condilion that is present for a minimum of %even calendar day’s, and that involves:
  LA period of incapacity or treatment connected with inpatient care (e.g., an overnight slay) in a
  hospital, hospice, or residential medical care facility; or
  2  .  A period of incapacity requiring absence of more than seven calendar days fi’om work, and that also
  involves continuing treatment by (or under the supervision of) a licensed health care provider; or
  3.  A period of incapacity’ (or for treatment) due to a chronic serious health condition (e.g.. asthma,
  diabetes, epilepsy. etc.): or
  4.  A period of incapacity that is long-term due to a condition for which treatment may’ be ineffective
  (e.g.. stroke, terminal disease. etc.): or
  5.  An absence to receive multiple treatments (including any period of recovery therefi’om) either for
  restorative surgery afier an accident or other irjury. or for a chronic condition such as cancer or
  kidney disease.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Continue the Public Hearing to hear public comment. 2. Close
the Public Hearing. 3. Discuss and determine appropriate action by either: a.) Affirming the action
of the Planning Commission; b.) Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other
evidence upon which the Commission made its decision, and after receiving such evidence take
such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; c.) Refer the matter back to
the Commission, with or without instructions for further proceedings; or d.) Continue the matter
for hearing on another date before itself, considered de novo. (Avalon Municipal Code Section
9-8. 60 1)

REPORT SUMMARY: This item was originally considered by the City Council during the June
8, 2022 regular City Council meeting. City Council requested more information from City Staff
and the matter was continued to June 21, 2022. At the June 21, 2022 City Council meeting no
new information or testimony was provided and the item was continued to this July 19, 2022
regular meeting of the City Council.

Per Government Code Sections 65905, 65091 and 65092 and other provisions of Planning and
Zoning Law, a public notice is required for notice of public hearings of the Planning Commission
regarding applications, revocations or modifications for variances, conditional use permits, or
equivalent development permits, or appeal of action thereon. Additionally, a public notice is
required if the proposed project affects permitted uses, or intensity of uses of real property.

The Government Code requires, at least ten days before a hearing. Notice is required to be
provided via:
  -  Mailing to real property owners within 300 feet of the subject real property on latest
  assessment roll; and
  -  Publication in a newspaper of general circulation; or
  -  Posted in three public places.
The City of Avalon utilizes information provided by the Los Angeles County Assessor’s Office to
determine property owners and the appropriate mailing addresses consistent with State law. It
is not unusual for property owners to have an incorrect mailing addresses, including but not
limited to listing their physical address in Avalon as their mailing address. City Staff cannot
manipulate the assessor list. The property owner must submit a change of address to the Los
Angeles County Assessor’s Office in order to correct the address.

On April 20, 2022, the Planning Commission took action on a request for approval of a Site Plan
(Section 9-8.201 et seq. of the Avalon Municipal Code (L(AMC!!)) and a Setback Variance at 261

The April 20, 2022 Planning Commission Staff Report noted the plans approved by the Planning
Commission on November 20, 2019 included the remodel of an existing nonconforming structure
encroaching up to three (3) feet of the rear property line and directly adjacent to the western
property line, where the standard setback requirement for this zone is ten (10) feet. The
subsequent new construction maintains a three (3) foot setback. The original construction plan
included remodeling the rear property with the intent of maintaining its nonconforming status.
However, after issued a building permit on September 14, 2021! it was determined that the
necessary improvements to retain the second building were infeasible! and the entire structure
was demolished.

AMC 9-8.703 (a) establishes: “A nonconforming building or structure may be continuously
maintained provided there is no alteration, addition or enlargement of any area! space or volume
of the structure  As approved! necessary improvements were considered infeasible without
demolition of the structure, and the original ‘nonconforming” structure and the proposed new
nonconforming structure maintained nearly identical footprints, City Staff recommended to the
Planning Commission during the March 16! 2022 and April 20! 2022 meetings that the setback
variance be granted as the renovated building complies with AMC 9-8.703 (a). The Planning
Commission accepted Staff’s recommendation! approved the Site Plan and Setback Variance
by Resolution 22-08.

On May 3, 2022 Charles Canby, and other surrounding property owners, filed a timely appeal of
the Planning Commission’s decision, requesting that the City Council hear the Project de novo
at a public hearing.

Article 8.6 of the Planning and Zoning Code (“Appeals”) states:

  a) Within 15 days after the receipt by the applicant for a variance or conditional use permit,
  or receipt by the owner or operator of a use which was the subject of a public hearing for
  revocation or modification! or notice of the action of the Commission! any person
  dissatisfied with the action of the Commission may file with the City Clerk an appeal from
  such action.
  b) Upon receiving a notice of appeal, the City Council may:
  1. Affirm the action of the Commission; or
  2. Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other evidence upon
  which the Commission made its decision, and after receiving such evidence take
  such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; or
  3. Refer the mailer back to the Commission, with or without instructions for further
  proceedings; or
  4. Set the matter for hearing before itself. At such hearing, it shall hear and decide
  the case de novo.

Staff supports the Planning Commission’s consideration and approval of the setback variance
and the finding made by the Planning Commission as the process complied with the appropriate
procedure and publically noticing process as outlined in the Government Code and AMC. To
confirm:
  ‘l
   1. The Planning Commission considered the request at two duly noticed regularly scheduled
  meetings (March 16, 2022 and April 20, 2022) and at both meetings they were able to
  consider all information provided by City Staff, including analysis provided in Staff Report.
  construction plans, and written comments provided by neighbors.
  2. Both duly noticed regularly scheduled meetings were open to the public at which time
  members of the public were able to provide oral testimony regarding the project for the
  Planning Commissioner consideration.
  3. The request was considered over two meetings to provide Planning Commissioners
  adequate time to thoroughly consider the request.
  4. Planning Commission adopted Resolution 22-08, granting the variance and noting the
  projects exemption for CEQA, compliance with AMC 9-8,203, and that the ‘structural
  footprint will remain almost exactly as it has existed since original construction.”

REPORT SUMMARY: On April 20, 2022, the Planning Commission of the City of Avalon took
action on a request for approval of a Site Plan (Section 9-8.201 et seq. of the Avalon Municipal
Code (“AMC”)) and a Setback Variance at 261 E. Whittley for the ongoing remodel of a duplex
in the Medium Density Residential zone, categorically exempt from environmental review under
Section 15301 of the State CEQA Guidelines Existing Facilities.
  —

The April 20, 2022 meeting was the fourth time the Planning Commission heard an issue
regarding the 261 E. Whittley Property:
  -  July 17, 2019 A Public Hearing was conducted for Site Plan review to renovate an
  —

  existing duplex with four bedrooms into a four bedroom single family dwelling. The project
  included the addition of 974 square feet.
  -  November 20, 2019 Application for a Site Plan! Height Variance (for a chimney) and
  —

  Costal Development Permit.
  -  March 16, 2022 A Public Hearing was conducted to consider a Setback Variance and
  —

  Site Plan review. Consideration of the request was continued to the next regular Planning
  Commission Meeting.
  -  April20, 2022— The Public Hearing was continued and a Setback Variance was approved
  via PC Resolution No. 22-08, which approved the Variance and Site Plan while finding
  the project exempt from environmental review.

The April 20, 2022 Planning Commission Staff Report noted the plans approved by the Planning
Commission on November 20, 2019 included the remodel of an existing nonconforming structure
encroaching up to three (3) feet of the rear property line and directly adjacent to the western
property line, where the standard setback requirement for this zone is ten (10) feet. The
subsequent new construction maintains a three (3) foot setback. The original construction plan
included remodeling the rear property with the intent of maintaining its nonconforming status.
However, after issued a building permit on September 14, 2021, it was determined that the
  1
 necessary improvements to retain the second building were infeasible, and the entire structure
was demolished. The owner’s intent was to move forward with the construction as previously
reviewed and approved.

AMC 9-8.703 (a) establishes: “A nonconforming building or structure may be continuously
maintained provided there is no alteration, addition or enlargement of any area, space or volume
of the structure..” As the approved, necessary improvements were considered infeasible
without demolition of the structure, Staff recommendation to the Planning Commission during
the March 16, 2022 and April 20,2022 meetings maintained that the renovated building complies
with AMC 9-8.703 (a). The Planning Commission accepted Staff’s recommendation, approved
the Site Plan and Setback Variance by Resolution 22-08.

On May 3, 2022 Charles Canby, and other surrounding property owners, filed a timely appeal of
the Planning Commission’s decision, requesting that the City Council hear the Project de novo
at a public hearing.

Article 8.6 of the Planning and Zoning Code (Appeals”) states:

  a) Within 15 days after the receipt by the applicant for a variance or conditional use permit,
  or receipt by the owner or operator of a use which was the subject of a public hearing for
  revocation or modification, or notice of the action of the Commission, any person
  dissatisfied with the action of the Commission may file with the City Clerk an appeal from
  such action.
  b) Upon receiving a notice of appeal, the City Council may:
  1. Affirm the action of the Commission; or
  2. Require a transcript or recording of the testimony, and all other evidence upon
  which the Commission made its decision, and after receiving such evidence take
  such action as, in its opinion, is indicated by such evidence alone; or
  3. Refer the matter back to the Commission, with or without instructions for further
  proceedings; or
  4. Set the matter for hearing before itself. At such hearing, it shall hear and decide
  the case de novo.

Staff supports the Planning Commission’s consideration and approval of the setback variance
and the finding made by the Planning Commission based on the following:

  1. The Planning Commission considered the request at two duly noticed regularly scheduled
  meetings (March 16, 2022 and April 20, 2022) and at both meetings they were able to
  consider all information provided by City Staff, including analysis provided in Staff Report,
  construction plans, and written comments provided by neighbors.
  2. Both duly noticed regularly scheduled meetings were open to the public at which time
  members of the public were able to provide oral testimony regarding the project for the
  Planning Commissioner consideration.
  3. The request was considered over two meetings to provide Planning Commissioners
  adequate time to thoroughly consider the request.
  4. On April20, 2022 Planning Commission accepted Staff’s recommendation to approve the
  Site Plan and Setback Variance.

  2
   5. Planning Commission adopted Resolution 22-08, granting the variance and noting the
  projects exemption for CEQA, compliance with AMC 9-8.203, and that the structural
  footprint will remain almost exactly as it has existed since original construction.”

FISCAL IMPACTS: Any expenses incurred by the City in the preparation of the appeal are
reimbursable by the Applicant.

be upheld, the project will not move forward as proposed. The applicant may revise the Project
to address any findings supporting the City Council’s denial.

To: City of Avalon Planning Commission Members and Staff

From: Charles Canby, 242 Whittley Aye, Avalon, CA

Subject: 261 East Whittley, granting of variance for setback.

lam against the Planning Commission granting a set back variance for the noted property.

  1.  I feel that we, residents of our neighborhood, have an expectation that planning and zoning
  rules will be followed and variances should not be granted to accommodate another person’s
  personal gains, desires and whims when they are unwarranted and to the detriment of others.

  2.  The proposed variance will shade the adjoining neighbors’ yards and homes and, will put a
  twenty-foot-high structure within three feet of their yards and view, and go against their
  expectation that when purchasing their property, buildings behind them would have a ten-foot
  set-back.

  3.  I have reviewed the plans for this project and looked over the property to gain an understanding
  of the project.

  4.  The area/yard where the Vaneverys want to build is a huge area with plenty of square footage.
  It is easily large enough to build a very large structure of equal square footage that they desire
  and still have open space for a yard without encroaching into the required ten-foot set back.

  S.  The Vaneverys want to encroach into the required setback. I speculate that they want to do so
  for a couple of reasons: First, to have a clear view of the ocean down the back lots of homes on
  East Whittley. Second, to not have to excavate or notch into the sloping hill side of their
  downhill sloping hack yard.

  6.  All of the existing homes on East Whittley have maintained the required ten-foot set back.
  Granting this variance could start a precedence.

  7.  The Staff report said “c) The Granting of this Variance will not be detrimental to the public
  welfare or neighborhood property because: The structural footprint will remain almost exactly
  as it has existed since original construction.” The short comings of this statement are: First,
  there are no original drawing or documentation showing the original construction. Second, the
  original structure was said to be much smaller and lower in elevation, and was not twenty feet
  high and three feet from the neighbors back yards. The old structure could not be seen from
  the back yards of the Warrens and Franks.

  8.  The set-back of the old demolished building was “non-conforming”. Now is an opportunity to
  build a conforming building without variances.

(a) Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take place
in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. The proposed project complies with
all the development standards for the Medium Density zone with the exception of the non
conforming setbacks the nexus of this Variance application.

The proposed project involves the remodel in a duplex by adding 125 square feet total divide
between three bedrooms changing the roof pitch from flat to pitched and adding two off

height envelope is perpendicular to the slope of the lot. The existing structure intrudes
beyond this perpendicular line. A portion of the roof deck railing and the deck on the third
level will be beyond this perpendicular line and thus need a height variance.

Commission make three (3) findings under Avalon Municipal Code Section 9-8.203. These
findings and corresponding explanations of the project’s compliance with these findings are

shall take place in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title.

density. The decks will require a variance, but is otherwise in compliance with applicable
provisions of Title 9.

  (b)  Every use, development of land and application of development standards
shall be considered on the basis of the suitability of the site for the particular use or
development in-tended, and the total development, including the application of prescribed
development standards, shall be so arranged as to avoid traffic congestion, insure the

neighboring property and shall be in general accord with all elements of the General Plan.
All of the surrounding properties are developed with single- or multi-family residences and
most of them have multiple decks on the face of the structures. The subject property and all
surrounding properties are designated for Medium Density Residential use in the Avalon

(a)  Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take

  the legal non-conforming status.

 (b)  Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall be

  effects on neighboring property and shall be in general accord with all elements of the

  The proposed project involves an existing duplex in the Medium Density Residential

  proposed project complies with the Avalon General Plan and its objectives of providing
  quality housing.

(c)  Every use, development of land, application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not
  intended that such approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of
  architecture.

  The exterior style of the building will be maintained. The functional development is
  suitable for a four (4) bedroom single family dwelling.

   Section 3. Pursuant to Section AMC 9-8.203, and based on the entire record before the
Planning Commission, all written and oral evidence presented to the Planning Commission and
the findings set forth below, the Planning Commission approved, subject to the conditions set
forth in Exhibit “A”, a Coastal Development Permit to renovate the exterior of a multi unit
residential structure to add 974 sq. ft. to modify the second kitchen into a mini kitchen laundry
for the use of guests.

(a)  The use is consistent with the goals and objectives of the public access and recreation
  policies of Chapter 3 of the California Coastal Act.

  The 974 sq. ft. will not change public access or recreational use of the coastal zone.

(b)  The use is in conformance with the Certified Local Coastal Program for the City of
  Avalon, which includes the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal Plan for Avalon, as
  well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances.

  The location is in the medium density zone and is a principally permitted use under
  Section 9-5.402. Based on the referenced code sections, the renovation to the exterior of
  the multi unit residential structure to add 974 sq. ft. does not trigger the need for a
  conditional use permit or variance. The addition of 974 sq. ft. will not expand the scope of
  the use to require additional staff or require inclusionary housing thus it is in compliance
  with the Affordable Housing Ordinances.

(c)  The use has received all necessary local approvals issuable by the Planning Commission,
  including Growth Ordinance Approval (in concept) together with water allocation, as
  may be required.

  The project is within the 2019 Growth Policy in the category of project described below:

  a) Projects involving existing commercial and residential structures which are to be
  repaired, replaced in kind, or remodeled or enlarged provided no additional bedrooms are
  added or dwelling units are added to existing residential structures other than the density
  bonus units permitted by conditional use permit and Southern California Edison Company
  confirms in writing that water is available to serve the project if approved by the city.

  SCE has confirmed that no additional water allocation is required

(d)  The use has been cleared with respect to environmental regulations of CEQA, as
  necessary.
